The devil will try to discourage you and get you to think you’re defeated, but trust God, keep doing what’s right, and watch God work out your story for His good!
new_believer.confession: God is good, and He is working all things for my good!

new_believer.verse_text: “As Jesus was getting into the boat, the man who had been demon-possessed begged to go with him. Jesus did not let him, but said, ‘Go home to your own people and tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and how he has had mercy on you.’”
new_believer.devotion: God has saved you and set you free, and now it’s your turn to go into your world and tell others the story of the goodness of God. Many people in your world may not come to church initially, but they can hear about Jesus and how He saves from you. You may feel like you’re not qualified to share your faith or lead someone to Jesus, but this man who was set free had no training; he simply had an encounter with Jesus. He was a witness to what Jesus did in his life. That’s the main thing that Jesus is asking from you—to tell your story!
new_believer.questions: How has Jesus changed your life? Who can you tell your story to this week? Who can you invite to church?
new_believer.confession: I will tell the story of God’s goodness and salvation in my life to the world around me.

new_believer.verse_text: “As for other matters, brothers and sisters, we instructed you how to live in order to please God, as in fact you are living. Now we ask you and urge you in the Lord Jesus to do this more and more.”
new_believer.devotion: The more you walk with Jesus, the more you’ll want to please Him with your life. It’s not something you’ll feel obligated to do; it’s just the natural response to His grace and goodness in your life. I love how the Apostle Paul calls us to take what we’ve been learning and keep growing more and more. Don’t stop and settle for your current level of maturity. This verse also reminds us that most of your faith journey won’t be a lot of new things you don’t know but continuing to develop and strengthen in the fundamentals of your faith.
new_believer.questions: What are a few of the key fundamentals of following Jesus you’ve learned so far? What’s one area you could grow in right now?
new_believer.confession: I will keep growing my faith and live to please God.!

new_believer.verse_text: “The seventh angel sounded his trumpet, and there were loud voices in heaven, which said: ‘The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Messiah, and he will reign for ever and ever.’”
new_believer.devotion: As we wrap up this book, it’s important to know that God has an ultimate plan to evict evil from the earth and reestablish His kingdom across the planet! Jesus won our salvation on the cross, and He will have the final victory over the devil and end his rule on earth once and for all. And all nations will submit to Jesus as our ultimate King and ruler. There will be no tribe or nation that’s outside of His rule. So you can rest in God’s plan and have great hope knowing that no matter what we face in our lifetime, God will bring judgment to Satan and restore the earth.
new_believer.questions: Are you confident in the future? How are you working to establish His kingdom on earth until He comes back?
new_believer.confession: There is one King, and His name is Jesus. He will reign and restore all the nations of the earth to Himself.

kids.verse_text: “In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.”
kids.devotion: The whole earth and everyone on it were made by God. He is the author and designer of all life. From the grass in the field to the eagle in the sky and ultimately to Adam and Eve. The Bible teaches us that God brought you into the world not by accident but with intentional design. Just like the designer of a house or car is the best to give details and instruction on how to operate that car, your heavenly Father is the best one to direct and guide our lives.
kids.questions: What’s your favorite animal that God made? What’s one place on earth you’d like to visit?
kids.confession: Our God is the creator of the heavens and the earth and the designer of my life.

kids.verse_text: “Your word is a lamp for my feet, a light on my path.”
kids.devotion: When it’s dark out and you’re trying to walk somewhere, you need to get a flashlight to light up the path so you don’t go off track or trip over something along the way. The Bible is our flashlight. Because of sin, the world is dark and confusing and only the light of God’s Word can clarify, make sense and show the way through.
kids.questions: What’s your favorite story or book of the Bible? And why? Maybe; King David, Esther, Paul.
kids.confession: The Bible is my guide along the path of life. If I follow God’s Word I won’t stumble in the dark.

kids.verse_text: “Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding; in all your ways submit to him, and he will make your paths straight.”
kids.devotion: Imagine trying to hold yourself up from falling by leaning on a small twig. That stick would break and you would fall. Now instead imagine keeping yourself held up by leaning against a solid brick pillar. That’s the difference between leaning on God’s understanding or your own. When you put your confidence in God’s thoughts and truth over your own then you’ll find that it keeps you upright and solid.
kids.questions: Did you ever have something break that you thought would hold you up? Do you trust God to take care of you?
kids.confession: God’s thoughts are greater than mine. I will always choose God’s ways over my ways.

kids.verse_text: “For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life.”
kids.devotion: Sometimes people talk about God as being angry at humans, and while our sin must be paid for, The Bible is clear that Jesus came because He loved us not because he was angry at us. No matter what happens in life, if you doubt God’s love for you come back and read John 3:16 and be reminded that God sent his very best because of His great love for you and all humanity!
kids.questions: Did you know that Jesus loved you that much? What family, friends, or teacher do you want to tell about Jesus and invite them to church?
kids.confession: I am so loved and valuable to God that Jesus was willing to come to earth and save me from the penalty of sin.

kids.verse_text: “Jesus replied: “ ‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.’ This is the first and greatest commandment.” And the second is like it, love your neighbor as yourself."
kids.devotion: The Bible is full of simple but powerful principles like this. If you correctly follow them, it makes the rest of life work the way God intended. So, Jesus is teaching us priorities. Loving God is the main thing and source of life. Obedience to what God says in the Bible is one of the greatest ways who show God we love him. And loving your neighbor and people around you is an overflow of your relationship with God.
kids.questions: What do you love the most about being a child of God? What’s one way you can show people you love them?
kids.confession: I will love God and obey His Word. He will have my whole heart. And I will choose to love others even when it isn’t convenient.

kids.verse_text: “Come near to God and he will come near to you.”
kids.devotion: This is one of my favorite promises in The Bible. It reminds us that God wants to be close to us. He’s not interested in just a long-distance relationship He wants to be near you. Notice also how God invites us to take that step of closeness with him. Some of the ways that we “come close to God” are by reading the Bible, spending time in worship, and taking time to pray.
kids.questions: What is your favorite way to spend time with God? Prayer? Bible reading? Church? What’s your favorite worship song?
kids.confession: My God wants to be close to me and invites me to talk with Him.

kids.verse_text: “‘Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us today our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.” for yours is the kingdom And the power and the glory forever and ever amen.”
kids.devotion: Jesus showed His disciples to pray, so we as His disciples today can also learn from it. First, you’ll notice Jesus show them to address God more personally as Father. He then shows us to not make prayer just about what we want but about God’s kingdom. Be intentional to pray for God’s will to be done in your city and nation. Then you focus on talking to God about your needs; He wants to hear and provide. Jesus shows us how important it is to forgive others and to invite God to help us fight temptation.
kids.questions: What’s something you need God to do for you? Did you pray about it? Is there anyone you need to forgive?
kids.confession: I will pray with confidence knowing my Father in heaven hears me. God hears and responds to my prayers. I will pray for God’s will to be done in my city.

kids.verse_text: “But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control.”
kids.devotion: Life is less about forcing things to happen and more about growing into what God has for you. An orange tree doesn’t try hard to grow oranges, it’s just what an orange tree does. If the roots and soil are good, the fruit will grow. In the same way, the fruit of the Spirit isn’t something we force but something that is a normal overflow of your relationship with Jesus. The more time you spend with God, the more fruit will flow.
kids.questions: Which fruit of the Spirit do you find most difficult? Which fruit of the Spirit is easiest for you to show?
kids.confession: As I spend time with Jesus and study The Bible the fruit of the Spirit will grow in my life.‬‬

kids.verse_text: “How great is the love the Father has lavished on us, that we should be called children of God!”
kids.devotion: You aren’t just partially loved or tolerated, you’re loved with an over-the-top kind of love. A love so passionate that it would move God to adopt you as a son or daughter into the family of God. You went from being an enemy of God in regards to your sin to being in the family with all of the privileges that come with being a child of the King.
kids.questions: Did you know that God brought you into His family? What’s one fun thing you want to do with God when you get to heaven?
kids.confession: I am a child of God who is greatly loved by my heavenly Father.

kids.verse_text: “go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything I have commanded you. And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age.”
kids.devotion: As followers of Jesus, we know that our lives are not just about living for our personal plans or dreams. But, in addition to our life goals, we have a larger vision from Jesus to share the good news to the whole world and to make disciples. Many live striving for meaning and value because all they focus on is themselves, but when you live for the greater purpose and the great commission from Jesus, you’ll find purpose, peace, and joy.
kids.questions: Did you know that Jesus asked you to make disciples? How can you show your friends how to follow Jesus? Who can you invite to church?
kids.confession: My mission is part of the larger mission Jesus gave us. I will live for more than just myself. I will show people how to follow Jesus.‬‬

kids.verse_text: “Therefore put on the full armor of God, so that when the day of evil comes, you may be able to stand your ground, and after you have done everything, to stand. Stand firm then, with the belt of truth buckled around your waist, with the breastplate of righteousness in place, and with your feet fitted with the readiness that comes from the gospel of peace. In addition to all this, take up the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one. Take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God. 18 And pray in the Spirit on all occasions with all kinds of prayers and requests. With this in mind, be alert and always keep on praying for all the Lord’s people.”
kids.devotion: When a soldier goes into a battle, they make sure to put on their armor and choose their weapons. In the same way, we are in a spiritual battle and must armor up. Satan wants to stop God’s plans and cause damage to God’s people, but we have been given powerful weapons and armor. We don’t have to be pushed around by the devil, we can rise, armor up, and defeat the enemy. God gives you both armor for protection and weapons to go on the attack against the enemy.
kids.questions: What’s your favorite part of the armor of God? Did you know that The Bible is your spiritual sword?
kids.confession: Jesus has given me authority over the devil. God gave us armor to defend against the devil’s attacks and gave us weapons to defeat him.

kids.verse_text: "Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged, for the Lord your God will be with you wherever you go.”
kids.devotion: Courage comes from knowing who your heavenly father is and knowing that he’s on your side. God will be with you. No difficulty or challenge can overcome you if the Lord is on your side. This verse shows us the fact that in life you will face difficult times and even discouraging times, but those challenges don’t have to cause you to lose hope because no matter the challenge God will always be with you.
kids.questions: What’s the bravest thing that you’ve ever done? What do you do when you feel afraid?
kids.confession: I will be strong and courageous. I will not back down from my purpose or calling no matter the challenge. The Lord is with me!

kids.verse_text: "God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.”
kids.devotion: When a tornado comes, we look for a storm shelter that is strong enough to protect us in the storm. In the storms of life, God has promised to be that place of refuge and covering. No matter what you’re facing, run to Jesus! The last part of that verse says that He is a “present” help, which means he is right there, he’s not distracted or distant from you but close to you. Not only is God close, but he wants to help and He is able.
kids.questions: The Bible tells us that God is all-powerful, He’s everywhere, He hears us and protects us. How does that give you the confidence to face life’s challenges?
kids.confession: I will run to Jesus not away from him in the difficulties of life. God is my help and strength.

kids.verse_text: "Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good; his love endures forever.”
kids.devotion: So often we base our thankfulness on circumstances being good, but King David understood the source of his thankfulness was not circumstances but the love of God. He had come to know that not only did God love and create you but His love is never-ending. It has no limit, no end and you can count on it. While God deals with evil very harshly, he deals with his kids with great kindness.
kids.questions: Was there ever a time you thought that God didn’t love you? Why did you feel that? Does God’s love ever end?
kids.confession: I will be thankful because God is good and his love never ends.

kids.verse_text: "I praise you because I am fearfully and wonderfully made; your works are wonderful, I know that full well.”
kids.devotion: God created the whole world in all its glory and He hand-formed and created you. You weren’t just thrown together but wonderfully and specifically made. Made in His image and made with incredible value and purpose. In life, you might find that people try to speak negatively about you or others because they don’t know their value. Learn to forgive them and continue to speak words of life over yourself and others.
kids.questions: What’s your favorite thing about how God made you? You are one of a kind! How do you think God will use you to change the World?
kids.confession: I will value my life and every human life. All people are hand-made by God in their mother’s womb with great intentionality and purpose.

kids.verse_text: "Walk with the wise and become wise, for a companion of fools suffers harm.”
kids.devotion: The friends that you hang out with the most are who you become like. We want to be friendly and kind to everyone but choose your close friends wisely. When we hang with people who are following Jesus then you’ll start seeing your life grow and be healthy but if you hang out with foolish people who keep making bad choices then you’ll find yourself doing the same.
kids.questions: Who is the smartest person you know? Are there any friends that have been a bad influence on you? How can you be a better friend?
kids.confession: My friends will impact my life for good or bad. I will choose friends wisely and I will grow to be a wise friend others want to hang out with.

kids.verse_text: "Do you not know? Have you not heard? The Lord is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He will not grow tired or weary, and his understanding no one can fathom.”
kids.devotion: Because we as humans get tired and sometimes overwhelmed we may unintentionally assume that God feels similar, but no matter what is happening in the world and your life, He’s not weary or tired in a physical way. He doesn’t need a break or a vacation, He’s fully ready and able to handle all that comes your way. This verse also reminds us that His wisdom and commands are beyond our understanding and our greatest form of wisdom is to trust His Word and follow it fully.
kids.questions: What’s the latest that you’ve stayed up without sleeping? God knows everything, what’s one question you’d like to ask God?
kids.confession: My God is strong and never grows tired. His ways and thoughts are true and higher than mine.

kids.verse_text: "For I know the plans I have for you,” declares the Lord, “plans to prosper you and not to harm you, plans to give you hope and a future.”
kids.devotion: Asking someone what they want to be when they grow up and what their plans are for the future can be common questions. But did you know that God has plans for you as well? He’s got a purpose and plan for your life and future. And the even better news is that His plans are always good! God doesn’t create us to leave us in pain or despair, but He created you with good plans in mind. In all of life’s circumstances, He is working out all things for your good.
kids.questions: What do you want to do when you grow up? What do you feel God is calling you to do? How does it make you feel that God has good plans for you?
kids.confession: God is good and He has good plans for me. I will walk in His ways and fulfill His purpose for my life.

kids.verse_text: “Do to others as you would have them do to you.”
kids.devotion: Our human instinct is to try and treat people the way they are treating us. If someone is rude or mean to us then we want to be mean back to them, but Jesus calls us to look past how we’re being treated and work to treat people how we would want them to treat us. This can be difficult, but you can with God’s help. It may take some time to change how people are treating you but start by focusing first on how you’re treating them and watch how God begins to change their heart and behavior.
kids.questions: Has anyone ever treated you badly? How did you respond? How do you want people to treat you?
kids.confession: I will treat others the way I want to be treated no matter how they are treating me.

kids.verse_text: "Each of you should give what you have decided in your heart to give, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver."
kids.devotion: The life of a believer should be marked by generosity. God gave everything on the cross and forgave everyone who had wronged him. He calls us to live in generosity in all things. God created the world to work best in response to your giving. Sowing and reaping. If we want to walk in the blessing of God then we need to develop a life and heart of giving.
kids.questions: What’s the best gift you’ve given to your family or friends? Do you find it hard or easy to give? Have you started giving your tithe (10% of income) to your church yet?
kids.confession: I love to give. God gave me everything and I will be generous and a blessing to others.

kids.verse_text: "Be kind and compassionate to one another, forgiving each other, just as in Christ God forgave you.”
kids.devotion: Forgiving someone who wronged you can often feel like something that they must earn or deserve, but Jesus calls us to radical forgiveness; showing grace towards others even when they don’t deserve it. Our command to forgive is based on Jesus forgiving us, not on whether or not others apologize for what they did to us. Since Jesus forgave you then you must also show mercy. Begin to pray for those who have hurt you and keep forgiving and showing grace to them.
kids.questions: What are ways that we can show kindness to others? Is there anyone that you need to forgive?
kids.confession: I am thankful for the mercy of God that forgave my sin. I choose to forgive those who have wronged me.

kids.verse_text: "Do not be anxious about anything, but in every situation, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God.”
kids.devotion: As a child of God, we’re able to take on the adventures of life differently than those who don’t have hope. Some may watch the news or hear about tragedies in the World and start freaking out, but you don’t have to be like that. When you start feeling anxious or afraid, get into the habit of going quickly to God. This verse reminds us that God wants us to bring our needs and request to him. God isn’t bothered by your asking. He sees your faith and trust to come to Him as a great thing!
kids.questions: Do you ever worry? What do you worry about? Have you brought that to God in prayer?
kids.confession: When I’m feeling afraid, I will go to God first! God wants to hear me pray and ask for help!

kids.verse_text: "I can do all this through him who gives me strength.”
kids.devotion: In the old cartoon, Popeye, he would get strength from eating spinach. But, for you and I, our strength to overcome is found in the strength that Jesus provides. And since we serve the God of the impossible that means that nothing is impossible if God has called you to do it. Trust God, and step out in faith! Even when the situation seems like it can’t happen, keep trusting God.
kids.questions: If you could do anything, what would you do? What’s something you want to do that you need God’s help with?
kids.confession: I will not speak fear when God has called me to faith. I will speak in alignment with God’s Word about my life and calling.

kids.verse_text: "Children, obey your parents in everything, for this pleases the Lord.”
kids.devotion: God has entrusted parents with the amazing responsibility to care for, protect and teach their children. And as a child, when you honor your parents and follow their instructions you’ll find a blessing in that and God’s grace on it. As we’re growing and learning the Bible, God has entrusted our parents with wisdom that is beyond ours, so trust God by first learning to obey your parents as they teach you the Bible.
kids.questions: Do you find it hard or easy to obey your parents? Why or why not? Why do you think it’s important to listen to your parents?
kids.confession: I love and honor my parents. I will obey my parents and grow up to be a great parent that shows my kids God’s ways.

kids.verse_text: "Be alert and of sober mind. Your enemy the devil prowls around like a roaring lion looking for someone to devour.”
kids.devotion: Some deny there’s a supernatural world with an enemy called Satan, but if we’re honest we can see evil today trying to harm humanity and we see that throughout the Bible. That might seem scary but the good news is that the Bible gives us some clues to how the enemy operates which gives us an advantage in defeating him in our lives. Remember that because you’re a follower of Jesus, the devil cannot defeat you. The verse above says that the devil roars “like” a lion, but we serve the true Lion of the tribe of Judah!
kids.questions: Did you know that with Jesus you have more power than the devil? Have you ever felt like you could feel something evil? Did you pray in Jesus’ name to stop it?
kids.confession:
There is a devil, but the Holy Spirit in me is stronger. 

I will walk in power and authority in Jesus name.

kids.verse_text: "We love, because He first loved us."
kids.devotion: I’m so thankful for this truth! God didn’t come to you and love you because you earned it or proved you were good enough for His love. He came to earth and died on the cross because He loved us! Jesus went first! And the love and grace and forgiveness we have all flow because He loves us. The love I can have for others is because I’m overflowing with God’s love.
kids.questions: How does that make you feel knowing that God loves you? Who is someone you can show love to today?
kids.confession: I am loved by God. I will love others as Jesus loves me.

kids.verse_text: “Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over, will be poured into your lap. For with the measure you use, it will be measured to you.”
kids.devotion: If you need to receive something or you need an increase in an area of your life, don’t focus on getting or keeping what you have, focus on giving. We must keep giving. It’s similar to farming. If you want more corn, then you need to give or plant corn into the ground. If you don’t plant then you won’t have anything to harvest. This verse reminds us as well that God always outdoes your generosity. When you give, he’ll bring it back into your life but with extra and overflowing.
kids.questions: Did you know you can expect a response to your giving? How can you be more generous to God and others? What is something you’re expecting?
kids.confession: I am generous like my heavenly Father is. I will give and God will multiply it.

kids.verse_text: “He has shown you, O mortal, what is good. And what does the Lord require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.”
kids.devotion: I love it when God spells things out in the Bible very specifically for us. Often God calls us to follow in faith without always seeing, but in this verse, He gives us specific things that God desires from us. To act justly, which is to do what’s right. To love mercy, which is to have a bend towards showing grace. And to engage with God in humility. Which means to look to God as your ultimate authority. Do those simple things and watch God’s favor flow in your life.
kids.questions: How do you know what the right thing to do is? Is there someone who made you mad that you need to show mercy?
kids.confession: I will do what is Biblically right. I will show mercy to others. I will submit to God and His Word.

kids.verse_text: “Do not be deceived: God cannot be mocked. A man reaps what he sows.”
kids.devotion: At first look, this verse might seem like a negative thing like God is watching and ready to make sure you reap bad things from your bad decisions. And yes, you will reap pain from the negative or sinful seeds that you sow, but this verse is also a promise. You can be confident that you will reap what you sow. When you keep sowing good, even if it takes a while,  you will reap good things. It may feel like your reward is delayed but this is a guaranteed principle that you will see the rewards of your effort.
kids.questions: Is there anything in your life you want to see get better? What can you start doing or sowing to see that happen?
kids.confession: I will reap what I sow. I will see good things in my life as I apply God’s good word.‬‬

kids.verse_text: “But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.”
kids.devotion: The most incredible news is that when Jesus left earth to take His place on the throne in heaven, He didn’t leave us alone, instead, his leaving would allow Him to send the Holy Spirit. When the follower of Jesus is baptized with the Holy Spirit there is an unleashing of new power and authority over the enemy. When you receive the Holy Spirit you’ll speak in tongues and that heavenly langue will bring you incredible closeness to God and the Holy Spirit will empower you to be His witness and to operate in the powerful gifts of the Spirit.
kids.questions: Have you been filled with the power of the Holy Spirit? Have you ever told someone about Jesus?
kids.confession: Thank you Holy Spirit for your power and joy. I will step out and activate the gifts you’ve given me.

kids.verse_text: “Do not conform to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what God’s will is—his good, pleasing and perfect will.”
kids.devotion:
This verse is one of the most important. Which pattern are you building your life on? Just like a construction worker needs blueprints and plans to build the house, in our lives, we build our lives based on blueprints. But the question is, where are you getting your plans? From the world? Or from The Bible? God’s plans will bring life but the devil’s plans or this world’s patterns will bring death. If you’ve been building with bad plans, choose today to throw those out and begin to embrace God’s plans for your life.

questionS

Have you ever started doing the wrong thing because of watching a friend or show? What patterns have you seen in media/movies that are the wrong pattern?
kids.confession: I will build my life according to God’s plans, not the current culture.

kids.verse_text: “For the Lord God is a sun and shield; the Lord bestows favor and honor; no good thing does he withhold from those whose walk is blameless.”
kids.devotion: God is our protector and covering and he desires to release all of His goodness in your life. In the beginning, God created absolute perfection for Adam and Eve to live in, which gives us a window into the heart of God to always give His kids the best. God doesn’t withhold any good thing. That doesn’t mean that we won’t have trials or struggles in life but know the heart and intention of God is always for good in your life.
kids.questions: What does it mean to walk blamelessly? What good things has God done for you?
kids.confession: I will walk in the favor and honor the Lord provides. I will walk with integrity.

kids.verse_text: “The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and instruction.”
kids.devotion: Any chaos in this world is the result of people not fearing the Lord. What does that mean to fear the Lord? It means to revere and respect and honor the Lord. It means to see that God and His thoughts take authority and priority over your own. When we as humans decide that we know better than God and reject the Bible as our guide then we’ll end up experiencing pain and brokenness that God never intended. Wise people build their lives on God’s truth.
kids.questions: Have you ever ignored the wisdom of your parents, pastor, or teacher? What happened? Who is the ultimate authority in your life?
kids.confession: I trust God and His Word above all other human wisdom. His Word has the final authority in my life.

kids.verse_text: “Jesus answered, “I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.”
kids.devotion: Many claim different pathways to God. But God gave us His Word to guide us to the true path. If there were many paths the Bible would have told us but the Bible reveals only one way to eternal life and that is through Jesus Christ. He is not a way, Jesus is THE way. He is the Son of God and through His blood spilled on the cross we now come to the Father.
kids.questions: Have you had any friends talk about other religions or ways to God? Have you made the decision to follow Jesus?
kids.confession: Jesus is the only way to the Father. I will follow Jesus and His ways my whole life!

kids.verse_text: “God blessed them and said to them, “Be fruitful and increase in number; fill the earth and subdue it. Rule over the fish in the sea and the birds in the sky and over every living creature that moves on the ground.”
kids.devotion: Every person is driven to find their purpose. While there may be specific and unique things that God will ask you to do, He has also given us the big picture of His will for all humanity. You and I have been given charge of taking dominion on the earth and expanding God’s Kingdom. We are not to just exist, but to be fruitful and multiply on the earth. Whatever God has given you or called you to, take that and grow it and make it better.
kids.questions: Did you know that God had a plan for all humans? What job have your parents given you? How can you do it better?
kids.confession: We are called to care for the Earth. We are called to rule the earth. I will increase and multiply what I’ve been given.

kids.verse_text: “Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.”
kids.devotion: Freedom is at the core of Christianity. When you see and experience freedom you know that God is in it. Wherever freedom is growing it means that Biblical principles are at play. But when there’s a restricting and controlling state, it means the devil is at work. This is true in governments but also this is true to your relationship with Jesus. Church or Christianity that is more focused on rules and human perfection usually means that we’re losing connection with the Spirit.
kids.questions: Freedom is what God is known for, what is something you’re known for? Have you invited the Holy Spirit to be with you?
kids.confession: The Holy Spirit brings freedom everywhere He is. I will not control but empower.

kids.verse_text: “The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy; I have come that they may have life, and have it to the full.”
kids.devotion: The devil is a thief and a liar. He plans to destroy and take your life. All sin and rejection of God’s truth leads to death in the spirit and the natural. Adam and Eve experienced this spiritual death. They didn’t die in the natural when they followed the devil but they died spiritually and were separated from God. But, when you follow Jesus you’ll find more life, and not just any life, it’s a full life! You’ll experience greater joy and peace.
kids.questions: Have you seen bad things happen to you or others when they follow the devil’s way? Jesus said He came that we would have an amazing life, what does that look like to you?
kids.confession: I will not follow the way of the enemy, but I will have and live the full life that Jesus has for me.

kids.verse_text: “Take delight in the Lord, and he will give you the desires of your heart.”
kids.devotion: Alignment with God’s heart releases the blessing of God. When we come to Jesus, he saves us, heals us, and sets us free to live in Him. Often when we come to Jesus our desires are more focused on ourselves and how it will benefit us. But, when you allow God to transform your heart, you’ll find that the desires visions, and dreams in your heart will be transformed. They may not change but those desires will be purified so that in their fulfillment it brings Glory to God and serves others along the way.
kids.questions: What’s your favorite part about following Jesus? What is something fun or meaningful you want to do in life?
kids.confession: My heart and desire is to do the will of God. I will serve others with what God has given me.

kids.verse_text: “Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will lift you up.”
kids.devotion: Don’t worry too much about “getting ahead.” Focus more on humbly serving God and others. When you live submitted to God then you’ll see God elevate and promote you in the right way and the right timing. Too often we try to self-promote and strive to get ahead but that doesn’t fulfill and never lasts. When God promotes you then nothing can stop you. The reason the Bible calls us to humble ourselves before God is because it’s a choice of faith to trust God’s goodness, timing more than yours.
kids.questions: Have you ever wanted to be famous? Should we focus on being popular or helping others? What does it mean to be humble?
kids.confession: I will trust God’s timing and promotion. God’s Word and timing are perfect.

kids.verse_text: “Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or terrified because of them, for the Lord your God goes with you; he will never leave you nor forsake you.”
kids.devotion: The lack of fear is not that there are not scary things. It’s that the God you serve is greater than anything you’re scared of. God will be with you and promises never to leave you. Allow this truth to stay close to you in all seasons of life. Whether in the valley in hard times of life or on the mountain top where everything is going well. You’re not alone, He will be with you.
kids.questions: Tell us about a time you felt the presence of God with you. What do you do when you’re afraid?
kids.confession: My God will never leave me on my own. Even in hard times He’s with me and will give me strength.

kids.verse_text: “Why do you look at the speck of sawdust in your brother’s eye and pay no attention to the plank in your own eye? How can you say to your brother, ‘Let me take the speck out of your eye,’ when all the time there is a plank in your own eye? You hypocrite, first take the plank out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.”
kids.devotion: We tend to focus more on the flaws and issues of our family and friends than on our issues. Jesus is teaching us to focus inwardly first when it comes to dealing with sin. When we try to do surgery on others while being blind it’s messy. First, allow God to do the work in your heart. Let Him remove those big logs and stones in your eyes. Then, you’ll be able to see clearly to help others. Your friends do need you to help them make changes but make sure you deal with your issues first.
kids.questions: Have you ever been guilty of being mad at your family or friends for something you do also? What is something you know God wants you to change?
kids.confession: I will deal with the sin and issues in my heart first. Lord, heal me so I can help others get healed.

kids.verse_text: “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.”
kids.devotion: It’s almost hard to wrap our heads around a perfect God who has always been and will continue to be. Since we are constantly changing and growing, we might assume that God is like that. But, his character and Word was, is, and will continue to be perfect. Which means it’s reliable. It’s something that you can put your confidence in. That’s great news even if we sin and mess up and even directly hurt the heart of God, he is not like us, he doesn’t end his love or mercy because we change, he is consistent in love and truth in all seasons.
kids.questions: Have you ever changed your mind on something? Did you know God never changes? How do you trust God?
kids.confession: God is perfect and never changes. His grace and truth are constant and forever. He is faithful even if I’m not.

kids.verse_text: “And without faith, it is impossible to please God, because anyone who comes to him must believe that he exists and that he rewards those who earnestly seek him.”
kids.devotion: I love this verse, it packs so much gold in it. First, we get a clue into how to live in a way that pleases God. I want to please God with my life and what is the key to pleasing God? Faith. He calls us into a life of faith and trust in Him. He calls us to believe and put action to our faith. A key display of your faith is to expect good from your heavenly Father. Faith is pleasing to God because it expects that God will respond and reward those who come to Him. Don’t come to God without the expectation that He’ll hear and respond!
kids.questions: What does faith mean? Do you believe that God responds when you pray? What are you praying and expecting God to do in your life?
kids.confession: I put my faith in God! He hears and rewards as I seek and follow Him.

kids.verse_text: “Every word of God is flawless; he is a shield to those who take refuge in him.”
kids.devotion: God’s Word is not just good ideas or interesting stories. The Bible gives us complete and perfect wisdom for life. Throughout the last several thousand years, scientific, historical, and psychological discoveries continue to echo and prove Biblical accuracy. No other document can be trusted like God’s Word. I love how it describes God’s Word as a protective shield. It’s true, when you live according to The Bible, it guards you against all kinds of evil.
kids.questions: Have you ever had to hide in a shelter during a storm? How does God’s Word shield us from life’s storms?
kids.confession: God’s Words are perfect. I will live according to The Bible’s instruction.

kids.verse_text: “Do nothing out of selfish ambition or vain conceit. Rather, in humility value others above yourselves, not looking to your own interests but each of you to the interests of the others.”
kids.devotion: What are you living for? Is life just about you and how you can get what you want? Is it just about how you can get ahead in life? The Bible calls us to live differently than that. We’re called not to live with selfish ambition but to live in a way that is focused on others before ourselves. That’s a little counterintuitive these days, but when you focus less on making yourself happy and more on serving others then you’ll find that God brings into your life all that you need and more.
kids.questions: Do you always play the game or watch the movie you want or do you let your friends choose first? What’s something you could do for your family or friends to help their lives be better?
kids.confession: I will live to serve others above myself. As I focus on others God will take care of me.

kids.verse_text: “Praise the Lord, my soul, and forget not all his benefits— who forgives all your sins and heals all your diseases, who redeems your life from the pit and crowns you with love and compassion, who satisfies your desires with good things so that your youth is renewed like the eagle’s.”
kids.devotion: We don’t serve and follow Jesus just for what He can do for us, but the truth is that there are incredible blessings associated with serving God. He forgives all your sin! That’s the most important and amazing thing. He heals all your diseases! What a promise of the supernatural overcoming our natural limitations. I’ve seen so many getting healed of pain from headaches to cancer. He Redeems you! Which means He won you back from the enemy! And He blesses and satisfies your life! These are just some of the incredible benefits to your life when you follow Jesus!
kids.questions: Did you know God can heal and forgive? Do you or someone you know need a miracle? Have you prayed?
kids.confession: Serving God brings with it great benefits in this life and the life to come. I am blessed and walk in His favor.

kids.verse_text: “But God demonstrates his own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
kids.devotion: God always goes first. He loves first, He forgives first! And Jesus displays the most unreal heart of God by dying on the cross for us even before we chose to follow Him. That’s how valuable you are to Him that He was willing to leave heaven and risk it all to bring you close to Himself again. This level of extravagance by Jesus is what drives us to live the same way. To take the love of Jesus and go into all the world and love others even before they deserve it.
kids.questions: Did God wait until you loved him before He died for you? Who has been rude to you that you can show grace to even before they are nice to you?
kids.confession: Thank you, Jesus, for dying for me even while I was against you and now I follow and surrendered to you.

kids.verse_text: “Flee the evil desires of youth and pursue righteousness, faith, love and peace, along with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart.”
kids.devotion: This verse is a huge key to living pure and in a way that honors God. When it comes to temptation, we need to focus more on running from sin rather than trying to fight it. The apostle Paul tells Timothy to run from sin. Joseph in the Bible runs from temptation. And in your life, stay away from people or situations that might lead you to sin. Instead, fill your mind heart, and attention with chasing after the things of God. Fill your life so full of the good things that you won’t have any room for sin.
kids.questions: Are there any sins that you get tempted by? How do you fight to keep doing the right thing even when you want to do the wrong thing?
kids.confession: I will live with purity before God. I will run from sin and run after the things of God.

kids.verse_text: “For it is by grace you have been saved, through faith—and this is not from yourselves, it is the gift of God— not by works, so that no one can boast.”
kids.devotion: How do we get saved? How can we pay the debt of our sin? It’s not in our hard work or good efforts but it’s by grace through faith. It’s by the Grace of God extended to us through Jesus. We put our faith in Jesus. This is the incredible free gift of salvation that is offered to us. Each person must decide if they are going to receive or reject this gift. If you reject it, you will live in hell eternally away from God. If you accept and put your faith in Jesus then you’re saved and secure and will spend eternity in Heaven with your heavenly Father as He intended.
kids.questions: Do we get to heaven by good works? Or by God’s grace? Have you opened that gift of salvation?
kids.confession: I am saved by God’s grace not my good deeds. I put my faith in Jesus and what He did on the cross.

kids.verse_text: “You shall have no other gods before me. “You shall not make for yourself an image in the form of anything in heaven above or on the earth beneath or in the waters below. You shall not bow down to them or worship them; for I, the Lord your God, am a jealous God, punishing the children for the sin of the parents to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me, but showing love to a thousand generations of those who love me and keep my commandments. “You shall not misuse the name of the Lord your God, for the Lord will not hold anyone guiltless who misuses his name.”
kids.devotion: The ten commandments that were given to Moses are the foundations of every healthy life and nation. When we embrace God’s ways of engaging Him and others, then we’ll build peace-filled and purposeful life and society. Jesus later sums up all the commands and laws into Loving God and loving others, but that’s built on the understanding about God’s desires for us to worship Him only and His command to treat others with dignity and respect. God’s commands always bring us life!
kids.questions: Is there anything in your life that you’re giving more priority to than God? How many generations does God show us His love?
kids.confession: I will put no other god before the one true God! I will honor others and live according to His commands.

kids.verse_text: “I have been crucified with Christ and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me. The life I now live in the body, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.”
kids.devotion: Before Jesus, we were trapped by sin and not just trapped but truly spiritually dead. Then Jesus came along and breathed life in us. He brought us back to life! And now, we’re no longer living for just ourselves but we’re living for and in Christ. This doesn’t mean that Jesus is going to tell you every little detail of your life and control you, but it does mean that you and I are living for His purpose and that you and I are yielded to God’s will as a priority. He gives you dreams and ability and wants you to run with it but have an open heart ready to pause, listen and respond to His leading.
kids.questions: What does it mean to be crucified with Christ? How do we live by faith? What has God asked you to do?
kids.confession: I will live each day to honor Jesus and build His Kingdom. Not my will by God’s will be done!

kids.verse_text: “Come, follow me,” Jesus said, “and I will send you out to fish for people.”
kids.devotion: This is the greatest and most incredible call in the Bible, to Follow Jesus! It’s what Jesus said to His disciples and it’s the same call that comes to each of us. First, the call is to come close to him, to walk with him to be near him to have a restored relationship. And secondly to be released out into the great purpose of fishing or reaching others with the message about Jesus. When you follow Jesus He will make something great out of you. He invites all to come as we are but He doesn’t leave us the way he found us.
kids.questions: When did you choose to follow Jesus? Or are you ready to do that now? Who are one or two people you’re praying to know Jesus and get saved?
kids.confession: I hear Jesus calling me to follow and I will respond with a massive yes! Wherever God calls me I will go!

men.verse_text: “Then the Lord God formed a man from the dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and the man became a living being.”
men.devotion: Our God is the most incredible designer; everywhere you look, creation is a megaphone for His power, creativity, and goodness. However, His best work is humanity. You were formed uniquely in His likeness; you carry an authority that no other creation has. God formed you to create, lead, and produce. The first man was given an assignment and a mission, and we carry that same mandate today. But God didn’t leave us on our own; He breathed His Spirit into us. We carry His authority and His power with us. Use it well!
men.questions: When was the last time you created something new? What is your primary calling and purpose? What are three key goals you’re going after this year?
men.confession: I am created in the image of God. I carry His authority and power. I live with purpose and intention.

men.verse_text: “But thanks be to God! He gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ. Therefore, my dear brothers and sisters, stand firm. Let nothing move you. Always give yourselves fully to the work of the Lord, because you know that your labor in the Lord is not in vain.”
men.devotion: We are followers of a great champion. Jesus is not a dead or conquered teacher but the creator and Lord of all the earth and the one who overcame sin and death. In that same winning and overcoming spirit, we as men have been called and commissioned. These verses call us to be unmovable! It’s an essential role of men to be the stabilizing force in a home and society. We are co-laborers with Christ and are called to lead our homes toward the work of the Lord.
men.questions: Do you see yourself as a winner or a victim? Do you stand up for others who are being oppressed? How do you handle pressure?
men.confession: In Jesus, I have victory over all the power of the enemy. I will not be moved by difficulty; I will stay in faith!

men.verse_text: “Be on your guard; stand firm in the faith; be courageous; be strong. Do everything in love.”
men.devotion: We are called to operate in strength and authority, but the great Apostle Paul called us to top off all of our courage and strength with love. True masculinity as God designed it knows how to be strong, but also to love strong. We are courageous because of love, not in spite of it. Jesus was motivated by love when He courageously came to rescue humanity. As the verses state, we defend, believe, and take our stand from the viewpoint of love. We discipline and correct out of love as well. The key is to consider what spirit you are operating in—fear, anger, jealousy, or love?
men.questions: Are you hanging out with men who inspire courage or fear? In what areas do you need to operate more in love?
men.confession: I am a man of courage who pushes past fear to walk in faith! I will do everything in love.

men.verse_text: “Then God said, ‘Let us make mankind in our image, in our likeness, so that they may rule over the fish in the sea and the birds in the sky, over the livestock and all the wild animals, and over all the creatures that move along the ground.’”
men.devotion: From day one, you and I were designed and called to care for and rule over the earth. God wants us to think big about our role. You’re not designed to be afraid of the world but to rule over it. Take the dominion of Jesus to every area that you rule: your home, your work, your city, and your nation. It’s important to see yourself as made and designed in His image and to take on rulership on His behalf. Do not wait around for God to do what He’s called you to do[^c0][^c1]; own your calling and lead on His behalf.
men.questions: What’s an area of your life that needs dominion? How could you grow and stretch in your personal, business, or ministry life? Where have you settled for less than God’s best?
men.confession: I have been formed in His likeness and am called to represent and extend His kingdom on earth.

men.verse_text: “Be alert and of sober mind. Your enemy the devil prowls around like a roaring lion looking for someone to devour. Resist him, standing firm in the faith, because you know that the family of believers throughout the world is undergoing the same kind of sufferings.”
men.devotion: Yes, we have an enemy that roars like a lion, but the good news is he’s not a lion. He will try to scare and harass you and ultimately devour you if you let him. He’s looking for someone who’s not paying attention and is unaware of the uppercut that’s coming their way. But in Jesus’ name, you have more authority than him. However, even though you have greater authority, he still has to be resisted. Today, stand firm in your convictions and in your authority as a son of God and resist the devil. Pray and command him to go in Jesus’ name!
men.questions: What areas in your life are most susceptible to the enemy’s attack? What are you doing to strengthen your stance against the devil?
men.confession: I am alert, aware, and ready to defeat the attacks of the enemy. I will stand firm in my faith and resist

men.verse_text: “Cast all your anxiety on him because he cares for you.”
men.devotion: As men, the weight of the world can feel like it’s resting on our shoulders. While God has designed us to carry the weight of our family, finances, and future, God invites us to partner with Him to bear the load. Feeling anxious or overwhelmed when we’re facing great pressure and new challenges can be common, which is why we must learn to cast those fears on God. You’ll find those anxieties fade as you spend more time in prayer, worship, and the Word. Spending time with God will remind you that He is greater than any challenges you’re facing.
men.confession: God cares about every detail of my life. I will bring my worries to Jesus daily in prayer!

men.verse_text: “Now the Lord God had formed out of the ground all the wild animals and all the birds in the sky. He brought them to the man to see what he would name them; and whatever the man called each living creature, that was its name.”
men.devotion: One of the first things God did with Adam before He brought Eve into his life was to teach him to name the animals. Whatever Adam called them, that was their name. It’s similar in our lives. God is going to teach you the power of the words you use and the labels that you put on people. Too often men grow up with fathers or father figures who didn’t know how to speak life into them, and then they repeat the cycle in their homes. If you want to have a home of joy, peace, strength, and confidence, then you have to learn to speak words of life.
men.questions: How do you use the power of your words? Have you learned to name your wife, kids, or friends in a way that is bringing life?
men.confession: I am thankful for life. I will use my voice to speak life over everyone in my world.

men.verse_text: “For physical training is of some value, but godliness has value for all things, holding promise for both the present life and the life to come.”
men.devotion: The decisions and choices we make hold within them different promises. In this passage, the Apostle Paul said the decision to be physically fit holds value for this life, and spiritual exercise holds promises for both this life and the next life. This isn’t a devotion to devalue exercise, because we should honor God by taking care of the body He gave so it can carry us to fulfill our purpose. But, when you look at the body and the spirit, it’s building up your spirit that has the most value. Working out your faith muscle is the priority.
men.questions: What are you doing to be physically healthy? What are you doing to grow your relationship with God? How are you prioritizing your faith?
men.confession: I will prioritize my relationship with God above all else. I will be healthy in mind, body, and spirit.

men.verse_text: “The Lord God said, ‘It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a helper suitable for him.’”
men.devotion: As men, we tend to be fine being on our own more often than women, but it’s not good for us to isolate. We’re designed for relationships, and the more we embrace great friends, the more we’ll find fulfillment and strength. We must surround ourselves with godly men who make us better, and it’s essential that we find a godly wife. Your wife is a partner and a complement[^c19][^c20] to you. It’s important that you embrace the full potential that your wife brings—not only for your sexual fulfillment but as a primary partner in your purpose.
men.questions: How can you increase the quality of people in your friend circle? How can you connect with your wife? Or if you are single, how can you prepare to find a wife?
men.confession: I will not do life alone. I

men.verse_text: “He humbled you, causing you to hunger and then feeding you with manna, which neither you nor your ancestors had known, to teach you that man does not live on bread alone but on every word that comes from the mouth of the Lord.”
men.devotion: God calls us into purpose and dominion. As men, we can get arrogant and start thinking our dominion is all our own doing. So, if you’re facing a season of testing and struggle, it may be God’s grace pulling you out beyond your own ability so you can learn to trust God again. We don’t overcome by our strength, but through God and His Word. His Word is life to us and feeds our souls and our bodies. Learn to go to God’s Word daily and watch your strength increase!
men.questions: Have you made reading or listening to the Bible a part of your daily routine? How do you best like to engage with the Bible? What’s a key thing that the Holy Spirit has been highlighting in your reading?
men.confession: I do not live by my strength alone; I am dependent on the Word of God for courage, hope, and life!

men.verse_text: “Know then in your heart that as a man disciplines his son, so the Lord your God disciplines you.”
men.devotion: God disciplines us because He loves us. He doesn’t want to see us left where we are but instead wants to challenge and call us out of our dysfunctions. God corrects us a few ways, through life’s circumstances and challenges, and sometimes He speaks directly to us to by His Word and Spirit.[^c49] This verse also challenges us to be good fathers who commit to disciplining our children. True love isn’t letting them live without correction; we must correct and develop them toward their purpose.
men.questions: How do you respond to correction? Is there a biblical mandate/command you need to obey? What is one area in which you need to discipline your child?
men.confession: I will be open and receptive to the discipline that God and my leaders bring into my life!

men.verse_text: “Am I now trying to win the approval of human beings, or of God? Or am I trying to please people? If I were still trying to please people, I would not be a servant of Christ.”
men.devotion: Who are you trying to please? One of the greatest dangers in life is trying to attain the approval of others. We should live in a way that fulfills our calling, and if we’re in school or on the job, we honor God by excelling at what we’ve been given. But working hard is different from working to earn your value. Your value is not something you earn; it’s something given to you by God. The more revelation you get from the Bible about your value and your secure position in the family of God, the more you can live with peace in your work.
men.questions: Do you primarily make decisions based on pleasing God, others, or yourself? How have you learned to break free from chasing the approval of others?
men.confession: I honor God and man, but I will live to please God with all that I think, say, and do.

men.verse_text: “For the word of God is alive and active. Sharper than any double-edged sword, it penetrates even to dividing soul and spirit, joints and marrow; it judges the thoughts and attitudes of the heart. Nothing in all creation is hidden from God’s sight. Everything is uncovered and laid bare before the eyes of him to whom we must give account.”
men.devotion: As men, we’re often the ones with the tool or weapon in our hands taking care of business, but have we opened up our lives to the sword of God? It’s not just any kind of weapon; it’s both powerful and precise. This weapon is the Word of God. It’s the thing that God uses to cut through the noise around us and get straight to the heart of the matter. It’s also the weapon that God gives us to use. When you take hold of the Word of God and begin to meditate on it and then speak it out, you’ll see your life transform and the devil flee!
men.questions: What’s the most challenging thing God is speaking to you right now? What verse are you meditating on?
men.confession: God’s Word is alive and active in my life! I will submit to and boldly speak the Word of God.

men.verse_text: “Therefore confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed. The prayer of a righteous person is powerful and effective.”
men.devotion: We often try to carry our issues and challenges on our own, but this will ultimately break us. God calls us to confess our sins to others so that times of healing can come. Yes, we first go to God with our sins, but being vulnerable and bringing our junk to the men in our lives will create the full process of healing, refreshing, and strengthening. You’re not designed to do life on your own. You’re not designed to face your battles on your own either. Confess your sins to a trusted friend or pastor, and watch your life and peace accelerate.
men.confession: I will confess my sin, submit to God, and pray powerful and effective prayers!

men.verse_text: “Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged, for the Lord your God will be with you wherever you go.”
men.devotion: We are commanded by God to be strong and courageous. Why? Because life can be overwhelming, and it’s a choice to live with courage. The difficult seasons that we face are going to constantly try to drain our strength. Don’t be caught off guard by the challenges of life. Feeling pressure and fatigue is normal; however, submitting to the pain and giving up is not what you were designed for. Your family and city are awaiting your courage. It’s why God intentionally sent you to earth in this hour. Be strong!
men.questions: Do you find it difficult to remain confident and courageous? How do you work to stir up courage in your life? What’s your greatest fear right now?
men.confession: I will not be afraid or discouraged by my circumstances; I will put my confidence in Jesus and boldly take action!

men.verse_text: “He answered, ‘“Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind”; and, “Love your neighbor as yourself.”’”
men.devotion: The strength of a man flows from his connection to his heavenly Father. Jesus reminded us that our primary focus must be to love and honor God with our lives. It’s the thing that should guide and govern our choices. If we make honoring God an afterthought, we’ll live spinning our wheels and chasing things that don’t matter. Jesus gave us a priorities prescription that will set up every area of our life to thrive. When loving God is not first, it creates chaos in the rest of what we do. Adjust your life to put loving God and others first.
men.questions: Is the life I’m building bringing honor to God and serving other people? Is there any part of my life that I’ve been holding back from God?
men.confession: I will love God with all my heart, soul, strength, and mind! Love for others flows from loving God.

men.verse_text: “He has shown you, O mortal, what is good. And what does the Lord require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.”
men.devotion: In this verse, God gets super clear on the values that He wants us to live by. We must act justly. This means that we’re walking with integrity in all that we do and in how we treat others. Then we are to love mercy. As followers of Jesus, we should be the most merciful people, giving forgiveness freely and an abundance of second chances. Finally, we must walk humbly before God. This means that we engage God from a place of submission to His way over ours. These three items are values to build your life on!
men.questions: Is there any injustice around you that you can fix? Is there anyone you can show mercy to? Is there any area where pride is sabotaging you?
men.confession: I will treat people fairly. I will extend forgiveness. I will honor God’s thoughts above my own.

men.verse_text: “The righteous lead blameless lives; blessed are their children after them.”
men.devotion: What you do and how you live matter. The choices that we as men make will impact those around us and will leave a legacy of strength or pain for our children. When we live righteously, which is in alignment with God’s Word, we’ll see our children blessed. Think of the difficulties that have been passed down to you from your parents. How have those battles been? And think of the blessings that have been handed down to you from your parents. Now, what do you want to pass on to your children? Each godly decision you make today will set the course for a new legacy for your family!
men.questions: Is there a dysfunction you don’t want passed down to your children? How can you live right before God?
men.confession: With God’s help, I will live a righteous and pure life. My wife, children, and friends will be blessed!

men.verse_text: “As iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another.”
men.devotion: When iron strikes iron, sparks begin to fly! It can be the same with us as men. When you’re in close connection and mentorship with another man, those times of discipleship and confrontation are the iron-striking-iron moments that cause us to be sharp. If we don’t like being challenged and confronted, we may try to avoid the discomfort of the sharpening, but that leaves us dull and ineffective. Lean into the tension. Put yourself in environments that challenge you to grow!
men.questions: Who are you being intentional to sharpen and mentor? Who are you speaking the truth to? Is there anyone who can call you out on your issues?
men.confession: I will not avoid confrontation or correction. I will embrace the input of my friends and mentors so I can grow!

men.verse_text: “The wise prevail through great power, and those who have knowledge muster their strength. Surely you need guidance to wage war, and victory is won through many advisers.”
men.devotion: Wisdom unlocks your power and potential. Many men try to push and strive their way through to victory, but those who are wise will listen to counsel, coaching, and advice that will allow them to unlock their giftings and abilities. Because victory doesn’t always go to the strongest but instead to the wisest, we must use wisdom to outwit our enemy. While we don’t face our enemies on a literal battlefield, they often come in the form of economic struggles, addictions, and challenges within work, relationships, and culture. We need wisdom to overcome!
men.questions: Do you have a coach to help you advance your business? Is there any battle you’re facing that you need to get input on?
men.confession: I will lead with wisdom and courage! I will seek the coaching of mentors before I charge into battle.

men.verse_text: “So, if you think you are standing firm, be careful that you don’t fall! No temptation has overtaken you except what is common to mankind. And God is faithful; he will not let you be tempted beyond what you can bear. But when you are tempted, he will also provide a way out so that you can endure it.”
men.devotion: We’d all like to think we’re invincible against sin and temptation, but if we’re honest, we each have areas of potential weakness. Now, what the devil would like you to think is that you’re abnormal and alone in your temptations. The truth is that, like the Bible says, it’s common. So, we need to learn to open up and invite other men into our world to help us break free and walk away from temptation. God will always provide a way out. God takes you through storms—but out of temptation!
men.questions: What’s the biggest temptation that you face? Have you opened up to another man about it? Have you asked God for strength and wisdom?
men.confession: I am not alone in my temptations. God has provided a way out, and with the help of my brothers in Christ, I will take it!

men.verse_text: “Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moths and vermin destroy, and where thieves break in and steal. But store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where moths and vermin do not destroy, and where thieves do not break in and steal. For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.”
men.devotion: Having an eternal perspective [^c66][^c67]is key to a fulfilled life on earth. Why? Because the eternal provides the context and purpose for this life. Many live aimlessly and, therefore, make no impact. But, when you live and do everything from a biblical perspective, it brings life into focus. The supernatural provides clarity for the natural. Making money is not what provides meaning; living a life of meaning and purpose is what will produce prosperity.
men.questions: Are you investing your money into the kingdom of God? How can you serve others? How are you making an impact with your work and life?
men.confession: I will store up treasures in heaven by investing my time and resources into the things on earth that are eternal.

men.verse_text: “Therefore, I urge you, brothers and sisters, in view of God’s mercy, to offer your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God—this is your true and proper worship. Do not conform to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what God’s will is—his good, pleasing and perfect will.”
men.devotion: What patterns are you building your life on? Every home needs blueprints for the crew to review and build from, and each of us is building our lives based on a set of patterns or blueprints. The challenge is that some people get defensive or protective about their patterns rather than checking and asking the question “Where did I get these blueprints, and are they working?” If our plans aren’t working, how do we course correct? It’s one thought at a time—by reading and applying God’s Word. Each time you apply it, it transforms you.
men.questions: Does your life look more like the world or like God’s Word? Is there any area of your life that isn’t working that you need to find God’s pattern for?
men.confession: I will give my life as a living sacrifice to God! I will not live for myself, but for Jesus and His kingdom.

men.verse_text: “Let us hold unswervingly to the hope we profess, for he who promised is faithful. And let us consider how we may spur one another on toward love and good deeds, not giving up meeting together, as some are in the habit of doing, but encouraging one another—and all the more as you see the Day approaching.”
men.devotion: Who are you inspiring toward good? Sometimes we’re taught to keep to ourselves and not interfere with someone else’s personal business, but that keeps us as bystanders and makes us useless to God. The truth is that we’re responsible to speak up for others and to encourage others in our world. Obviously, if you try to help someone and they don’t want it, that’s up to them, but if you see that they need help and do nothing, then that’s going to fall back on you. We have a responsibility to speak the truth to our world.
men.questions: Name three people who you can encourage today. Are you consistently taking yourself and your family to church? Are you and your family serving at church?
men.confession: I will speak the truth that people need. I will encourage others toward good works.

men.verse_text: “My dear brothers and sisters, take note of this: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak and slow to become angry, because human anger does not produce the righteousness that God desires.”
men.devotion: Often our frustrations or anger can be the result of not taking time to listen before we jump to conclusions. Taking the time to slow down, gather more information, and then make a call is huge. Not only do quick judgments lead to wrong or harmful assumptions, but they breed frustration and anger in your children. We lose trust with our friends, kids, and wife when we jump to conclusions and lose our temper. Don’t take things personally; step back, listen, and respond in a way that will be helpful.
men.questions: Do you have a difficult time not jumping to conclusions? Do you assume the best or worst about people? How would you rate your listening ability? [^c82]
men.confession: I will focus on the best in others. I will be patient and listen before I speak into a situation that frustrates me.

men.verse_text: “But you, man of God, flee from all this, and pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, endurance and gentleness. Fight the good fight of the faith. Take hold of the eternal life to which you were called when you made your good confession in the presence of many witnesses.”
men.devotion: As a man after God’s heart, it’s not just about fleeing sin but about what we’re pursuing. All of the great men of faith in the Bible aren’t in there because they didn’t sin. As a matter of fact, there are some pretty horrific things that many of them did in their lives. But, they were all marked by qualities of repentance, grace, pursuing justice, defending the oppressed, and establishing God’s kingdom. Don’t make your goal to just not do the wrong things; make it your goal to pursue the list the Apostle Paul gave to Timothy in these verses. As you chase after the right things, you’ll find your desire for sin will fade.
men.questions: What boundaries can you set to keep yourself away from sin? What good habit are you working on today?
men.confession: I hate sin and love God’s Word. I will live with purity, faith, and courage.

men.verse_text: “Jesus called them together and said, ‘You know that those who are regarded as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their high officials exercise authority over them. Not so with you. Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant, and whoever wants to be first must be slave of all. For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.’”
men.devotion: As men, we’re called to lead in our homes and in our world. Jesus set the example and called us to lead by serving. This simple but powerful approach will take your impact to a new level with your family, coworkers, staff, and the world around you. Servant leadership changes how you engage people. Rather than seeing those in your world as a stepping stone to where you want to go, you begin to see your role as helping others get to where they’re called to go. God design in life is for you to succeed when you help others win.
men.questions: Is there an area of your life where you could step into more of a leadership role? How are you doing with serving your wife? Kids? Clients?
men.confession: I will not hold back from a leadership role in my family, work, and church. I will help others succeed.

men.verse_text: “Blessed is the one who does not walk in step with the wicked or stand in the way that sinners take or sit in the company of mockers, but whose delight is in the law of the Lord, and who meditates on his law day and night. That person is like a tree planted by streams of water, which yields its fruit in season and whose leaf does not wither—whatever they do prospers.”
men.devotion: The key to prospering is to make God’s Word the focus and meditation of your heart and mind. That means it’s the central and core guidance of your life. When you make God’s Word your focus, it will begin to shape your life and decisions. When you make biblically based decisions, you’ll find that your life begins to grow and stay fresh like a tree planted by the water. That tree thrives because it’s getting consistent nutrients that the water brings; in the same way, God’s Word brings fresh insight that causes you to grow!
men.questions: Are you a part of the community at your local church? How often are you feeding on God’s Word? How would you describe your circle of friends?
men.confession: I will plant my life close to God’s Word and His people so I can thrive in all that I do.

men.verse_text: “The Lord is with me; I will not be afraid. What can mere mortals do to me? The Lord is with me; he is my helper. I look in triumph on my enemies. It is better to take refuge in the Lord than to trust in humans. It is better to take refuge in the Lord than to trust in princes.”
men.devotion: The Lord is with you! This truth will create peace and confidence through seasons where it feels like life and people are against you. The Bible reminds us that you don’t need to fear humans and what they can do to you; you just need to fear God and what He can do. No plan of man can override the plan that God has for you. While we honor and serve people, we do not live in fear of them or metaphorically bow to their pressure. Put your trust in God!
men.questions: Where have I been putting too much trust in people for my provision, peace, and purpose? Do you go to God or people first when trouble comes?
men.confession: God is with me so I will not fear! I will put my hope and confidence in God.

men.verse_text: “I have told you these things, so that in me you may have peace. In this world you will have trouble. But take heart! I have overcome the world.”
men.devotion: Jesus doesn’t promise us a life of ease, but He does promise a life of peace. When your mind and attention are focused on and consumed by the challenges and difficulties of this life, fear and hopelessness begin to rise.
